published_prior_art.cite: choiKwonLiao2024NoSplit: no-split low-rank completion uses a distinct nuclear-norm initialization plus least-squares factor refits, not serial second-order transfer for a masked proximal fixed point.
choiYuan2024MNAR: subgroup inference for deterministic-MNAR completion provides the q=0, one-date reduction, not finite-lag curvature correction and growing-window Wald inference.
choiYuan2024MNAR; choiYuan2025WeakFactors: separate sufficient weak-signal regimes for masked completion and dependent-noise PCA, not a matched native-optimizer signal-cohort-window frontier.

soundness_flags.label: prop:rankone-serial-drift
soundness_flags.one_line: The rank-one calibration does not specify normalized left/right factor sequences, aspect and preperiod ratios, or the penalty sequence, so the asserted limit psi·E[q_it]→-1 is not determined by the stated model.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives subgroup asymptotic-normality results for its deterministic-MNAR completion construction and a feasible variance estimator; the displayed subgroup result is indexed by a fixed target date.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Title page and abstract; estimator description in the introduction
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published article establishes no-sample-splitting inference for low-rank completion, using nuclear-norm penalization followed by least-squares factor/loading refits.

The article studies PC consistency and asymptotic normality for weak factors under suitable dependent-noise conditions; it is a fully observed factor-analysis comparator rather than a deterministic-block completion theorem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Specify a complete rank-one triangular-array calibration—factor normalizations, N:T:m:g:H ratios, lambda sequence, and the precise alternating right-factor formula—then state the drift constant as a function of those primitives before retaining the -1 limit.

Promote the phase-frontier OEQ into a field-strength matched statement by naming the first uncorrectable remainder on each face and fixing an explicit relatively open Gaussian MA(q) witness family for it.

Add a concise comparison table locating the exact Choi--Yuan subgroup theorem assumptions and conclusion against the proposed q>=1, growing-H result, including which restrictions are retained and which are genuinely enlarged.

recommended_next_step: Revise the under-specified rank-one calibration proposition, then advance the otherwise field-novel native-optimizer inference kernel to Stage 0.
